audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while the content layer reads Irelia x6 then Ekko — a cross-layer disagreement on all seven rows.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer, and phases[0..5].why already describe Irelia winning those stages. The full layer was stale.
audit.corrected: phases[0..5].side -> Irelia, phases[6].side -> Ekko, with the level-6-plus rating and why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chronobreak was described as 'a delayed rewind, not a combat tool' and the advice was to not respect it.
audit.why: Chronobreak makes Ekko untargetable during the rewind, heals him for a percentage of damage taken in that window, and deals massive damage around his arrival. It is 110/80/50s — the rank-3 cooldown is what makes the late game his.
audit.corrected: Stated the untargetability, the heal (and therefore Grievous Wounds), and the 110s-to-50s cooldown swing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase Dive's auto-attack reset was never mentioned, Parallel Convergence's shield was never mentioned, Timewinder was called 'long cooldown', and early claimed Ekko has 'no reliable escape before 6'.
audit.why: Phase Dive is a 325-range roll into a teleporting auto-reset on 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s — the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell. Parallel Convergence is 22/20/18/16/14s at 1600 range and both stuns and shields him when he enters the anomaly. Timewinder is 9s, not long. Irelia's E both stuns and grounds, which denies Phase Dive's blink.
audit.corrected: All four written in, with the E-grounds-Phase-Dive interaction stated as the decisive one.

audit.why: Chronobreak 110/80/50s, Parallel Convergence 22s, Timewinder 9s, Phase Dive 9s.
audit.corrected: Written in with the hold-your-finisher sequencing.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to their titles using Phase Dive and the wave-as-dashes logic.

edits.after: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat — your E grounds Phase Dive too.

edits.after: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 — track the hologram, hold your finisher, and the whole window after it belongs to you.

edits.after: Phase Dive is an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is your tell, so step back on the charge, then E-stun where he lands, not where he stood.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Defiant Dance has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 and only 50s at rank 3 — he is untargetable through the rewind and heals off the damage you just dealt, so hold your finisher until the hologram resolves. - Parallel Convergence is 22s and has to be armed early. - Timewinder and Phase Dive are both 9s.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Ekko wins by arming Parallel Convergence under you, stunning into a Phase Dive reset, and rewinding out of the answer.

edits.before: If Ekko takes first blood, tighten up: Chronobreak is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Ekko takes first blood, stop trading into a pre-armed Parallel Convergence — the anomaly stuns and shields him. Farm what Bladesurge reaches, buy Grievous Wounds for the Chronobreak heal, and re-enter on its 110s window.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by forcing the rewind early: bait Chronobreak with a half-commit and the next 110s of skirmishes have no undo.

edits.before: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, stun the carries, and let the marks ground the peel.
edits.after: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, E-stun the carries, and let R's wall slow whoever peels.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Ekko's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, punish the arm-up: he cannot place Parallel Convergence with you inside 600 range, and the rewind still costs 110s.

edits.before: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions — every one is a dash and the crash is an all-in announcement you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane — no minions, no dashes, no Irelia. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions between you and him — each is a Bladesurge and the crash is an all-in you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane, where Timewinder pokes from 1075 and you have nothing to dash to. Crash timing: crash while Parallel Convergence is unarmed — buy a plate, a reset, or a roam.

edits.before: Ekko has no reliable escape or answer to melee pressure at level 1, so early trades already favour your engage
edits.after: Ekko has only a 325-range Phase Dive and no answer to melee pressure early, so level 1 trades favour your engage

edits.before: Chronobreak is a delayed rewind rather than a combat tool, so Vanguard's Edge still wins the level 6 all-in
edits.after: Chronobreak needs a few seconds of history to rewind into, so a fast Vanguard's Edge all-in still wins level 6

edits.before: Ekko's Timewinder has a long cooldown and his W stun zone takes a second to arm, so a level 3 all-in the instant he throws Q and misses punishes him hard.
edits.after: Timewinder is only a 9s cooldown, but Parallel Convergence is 22s and must be armed in advance, so a level 3 all-in the instant that zone is down punishes him hard.

edits.before: Chronobreak is a delayed-rewind escape, not a combat tool, so Vanguard's Edge still lets you burst him down before he can bail with the ult.
edits.after: Chronobreak turns him untargetable and heals off your damage, so bait it with a half-commit at 6, then Vanguard's Edge finishes the real all-in.

edits.before: Ekko is a skillshot-reliant mage with no reliable escape before 6, and Timewinder's real cooldown means every miss is a wide open window to dash in and punish. His W stun zone needs to be pre-placed and armed, which telegraphs his all-in attempt — walk around it or force the fight before he can set it up. Push the wave and threaten trades on cooldown; he has nothing to answer sustained melee pressure pre-6.
edits.after: Ekko's only escape before 6 is a 325-range Phase Dive on 9s, and Timewinder sits on the same 9s, so every miss is a wide open window to dash in and punish. Parallel Convergence has to be pre-placed and armed on a 22s cooldown, which telegraphs the all-in — walk out of the circle before it detonates. Push the wave and threaten trades on cooldown; he has nothing that answers sustained melee pressure pre-6.

edits.before: Chronobreak sounds scary but it's a delayed rewind, not an instant escape or combat tool — if you commit to the all-in fast enough, Vanguard's Edge still gets you the kill before he can blink back to safety. Keep initiating the moment his Q or W is down, and don't respect Chronobreak as if it were a Zhonya's; it only saves him if he predicted the damage in advance. Roams are roughly even, so contest based on wave state rather than his ultimate.
edits.after: Chronobreak is real: he goes untargetable through the rewind and heals off the damage you just dealt, so a half-commit that only bails him out is still a win — the next 110s has no undo button in it. Keep initiating the moment Timewinder or Parallel Convergence is down, hold your finisher until the hologram resolves, and buy Grievous Wounds so the heal returns a fraction of what he expects. Roams are close to even, so contest on wave state.

edits.before: Once Ekko builds into Zhonya's and Riftmaker, his combo becomes genuinely safe and hard-hitting, and his rewind window covers mistakes that used to be free kills for you — this is the one phase where his kit outpaces yours. Play around his cooldowns rather than his general presence, and don't force a fight into a fresh W zone; the burst trade finally favours him once he's fully scaled.
edits.after: Once Ekko builds Zhonya's and Riftmaker his combo becomes genuinely safe and hard-hitting, and a 50s Chronobreak covers mistakes that used to be free kills for you — this is the one phase where his kit outpaces yours. Play around his cooldowns rather than his presence, never force into a freshly armed Parallel Convergence, and keep Grievous Wounds up so the rewind heal cannot undo the trade.
